rationale: The record is an empirical qualitative interview study of child welfare lawyers, judges, and social workers examining street-level bureaucratic discretion regarding housing adequacy in U.S. child welfare cases. It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access or any water/sanitation access outcome (E01: wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both the narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings because the study fails Criterion 1 and Criterion 4 entirely: it examines street-level bureaucratic discretion in child welfare and housing adequacy decisions rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: This article reports data from a qualitative study exploring perceptions of child welfare professionals about housing-related child welfare decisions.
Interviews were conducted with a purposive sample of 18 child welfare lawyers, judges, & masters level social workers from a large city in the mid-Atlantic U.S.
